footer.about: We're a locally owned and operated HVAC and plumbing company in Wichita. We repair and install heating and cooling equipment, and we repair and replace plumbing.
why: Extended warranties on high-efficiency A/C and heating equipment
Your customers already make your case. You hold a 5.0 on 131 Google reviews, and they say it plainly: "When my air conditioner stopped working on a Friday, I called and they were here that same day."
Your website tells a thinner story: a phone visitor must open the menu to tap your number, and nothing at the top says HVAC company in Wichita.
So we built this site around their words.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the HVAC Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page: what your site does today, and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: The top of the page says "Alpha HVAC & Plumbing" and nothing more, so Google can't tell you're an HVAC company in Wichita.
On a phone, your number hides in the menu, and the one at the very bottom of the page is plain text, not a button.
The review box shows 48 of your 131 Google reviews, under a different business name than Google's.
"Click on a brand below" invites a click on six logos, and nothing happens.
fixes: A headline that says HVAC company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
Your number one tap away at the top of every page, on a phone.
Reviews on every page, each beside the point it proves.
cards.alsoAdd: Every page set up behind the scenes so Google and AI tools like ChatGPT know exactly what you do, where you work, and what your customers say.

cards.title: AC Repair
cards.why: Your customers call when the AC quits, and this page gives them little.
problems: Cooling is one short block and three bullets, so someone whose AC quit today finds no page about it.
No photos of your work and no list of towns.
fixes: A full page for AC repair in Wichita, KS, with your 24-hour emergency line.
Reviews on fast response and clear explanations, each beside its point.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Furnace Repair
cards.why: Heating is half of what you do, and it shares one thin page.
problems: Heating is one short block and three bullets, with nothing for a furnace that stopped on a cold night.
No photos of your work and no questions answered.
fixes: A full page for furnace repair in Wichita, KS, from the cold-night call to the new install.
Reviews from customers who got heat back.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn’t think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a ready customer reaches you.
problems: A public "Site Under Maintenance" page shows a different phone number and a personal Gmail address.
An empty "Test for Reviews" page is public too.
fixes: One number and one business email, everywhere.
A short list of what to have ready.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already call you their go-to. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we'll walk you through this demo and plan your new site.

onboardingQuestions: Who owns the business, and what is the owner's full name? Tom Tallon is named most in reviews as the quote and office contact (the site's email is tomt@alpha-heatair.com). What is his role, and how should the site introduce him?

What is the legal name: Alpha HVAC and Plumbing LLC (Google), Alpha Heating & Air Conditioning, LLC (the site's review box and BBB snippet), or something else? Which one goes on the site and the Google listing?
Which of Goodman, Amana, Bryant, Daikin, Ruud and LG are they a certified or authorized dealer for? Can they send the dealer letter or locator listing? Until then the site shows no brand claims.
When was the company founded, and is it veteran-owned (a chamber directory snippet says so; the company's site does not)?
What is the 316-765-4492 number and the alphahc16@gmail.com address on the leftover "Site Under Maintenance" page? Is either one live, and should the page come down?
Are they licensed and insured in Kansas and Wichita, for HVAC and for plumbing? License numbers for the footer if so.
Maintenance plan: name, price, number of visits and what each visit covers (reviews call it the annual service plan, yearly service contract and maintenance agreement).
Wisetack financing: what terms, and for which jobs?
Which towns do they serve outside Wichita? The site says only "Wichita and all surrounding areas".
Street address: Google shows 3101 W Harry St, Wichita, KS 67213; a BBB snippet shows 1405 S Bebe St. Which is current, and should an address appear on the site?
Is the 24-hour emergency line the same (316) 260-5775 number? Does it ring through after hours, and is there an emergency fee?
Is there a Saturday or Sunday schedule? Reviews mention Saturday and Sunday visits, but the site lists Monday to Friday only.

Mini splits and ductless: do they install and repair them? Reviews mention a whole-home mini split install and a leak found at a mini split head. Heat pumps, ductwork and air purification systems also appear in reviews: confirm each.
Plumbing scope: drain cleaning, sewer backups, water lines and repiping, and tankless water heaters all appear in reviews or nowhere. Which should be listed?
Do they pull City permits and handle the City inspection and utility rebates (Evergy) on installs? One review says so; is it standard?
Do they take pictures of every system on a service visit, and wear shoe covers? Reviews say so; confirm before the site states it as standard.
Is equipment American-made? Two reviews say so, one naming Amana. Which brands do they install?
What does "100% Customer Satisfaction Guaranteed" cover, in writing?
Residential and commercial: what kinds of commercial work (apartment complexes, rentals, offices)?
Which Facebook page is the real one: facebook.com/alphahvacict or the profile.php?id=61575954281986 page? Do they want the second one removed?
Do they want the test page removed and the site's review count updated from 48 to the Google count?
Google shows 131 reviews, and 102 were pulled. Can they give us access to the rest, and permission to quote reviews on the site?
Logo file, brand colors and photos of real jobs and the team.
